Good question — timing and selection of “abs” work after a C‑section must balance healing, pelvic‑floor recovery, and diastasis recti (DR) risk. Below is a clear, practical guideline you can use with your client to decide when and how to reintroduce core exercises safely, plus a progressive 12‑week core return plan you can layer into the strength programme I already gave.

Important medical caveats
- Only begin abdominal work once her OB has cleared her for progressive activity at the 6‑week check (often the minimum). Even then, proceed gradually.
- If she has any of the following, delay core progression and refer to a pelvic‑floor physiotherapist:
  - Urinary/fecal incontinence, pelvic heaviness or bulging.
  - New or worsening pain with exercises.
  - Noticeable doming or coning along the midline during exertion (sign of DR).
  - Concern about incision tenderness or adhesions.
- If diastasis recti is present, prioritize transverse abdominal (deep core) retraining and pelvic‑floor rehab before heavy superficial abdominal loading.

When to add abs work — practical timeline
- Weeks 0–6 (postpartum, pre‑clearance): no direct abdominal loading. Focus on breathing, pelvic‑floor activation, posture, and gentle pelvic tilts only.
- Week 6 (after OB clearance): begin low‑load, deep core and pelvic‑floor re‑education — light activation only (see Week 6–8 below). Continue to avoid crunches, straight leg raises, heavy valsalva and intense trunk flexion.
- Weeks 7–10: progressive reintroduction of safe core exercises emphasizing transverse abdominis (TA), oblique control, and anti‑extension/rotation before flexion. Monitor for doming and symptoms.
- Weeks 11–12+: introduce some moderate‑intensity anterior core work (short planks, gentle curl patterns) if no doming, no leakage, and pelvic floor is strong. Heavy loaded abdominal exercises (weighted sit‑ups, full V‑ups, heavy Pallof presses with breath holding) should wait until pelvic floor clearance — commonly 12+ weeks and ideally after physiotherapist sign‑off.

How to screen before adding abs work (brief tests)
- Hook‑lying (supine, knees bent) breath test: can she breathe diaphragmatically (rib expansion) without bearing down or bulging?
- Heel slide test: supine, knees bent, slide one heel out slowly and return without doming — if she can do 8–10 slow controlled reps with no bulge, that's a good sign to progress.
- Gentle cough test: supine or standing, can she cough without urine leakage? If not, delay progression and refer.
- Palpation for DR: gentle fingers at midline while lifting head slightly — if separation >2–3 fingers and there is significant doming, progress conservatively and seek physio guidance.

Progressive 8‑week core return plan (start only after 6‑week clearance)
Overview: Start with 2–3 short core sessions/week integrated into strength days. Always couple core work with breathing and pelvic‑floor cues. Stop any exercise that causes doming, pain, or leakage.

Phase A — Weeks 6–8: Deep core re‑education and anti‑extension
Goals: retrain transverse abdominis and pelvic floor; improve coordination and breath control.

Exercises (low load)
- Diaphragmatic breathing with pelvic‑floor cue: 4 × 5 slow breaths (inhale diaphragmatically, gentle 2–3 sec pelvic floor lift on exhale).
- Supine abdominal brace: lying on back, knees bent, lightly draw belly button toward spine without flattening or holding breath — hold 5–8 sec × 6–8 reps.
- Heel slides (small range): 2–3 sets × 8–10 per side — maintain neutral pelvis.
- Bent‑knee fallouts (slow hip drops with bracing): 2 × 8 per side.
- Dead bug (hands support overhead small ROM) — knees bent: 2–3 × 8 per side (stop before any doming).
- Modified side plank from knees (short holds): 2 × 15–20 sec per side if no doming.

Phase B — Weeks 9–10: Build endurance and anti‑rotation control
Goals: increase load on core through anti‑extension and anti‑rotation patterns; introduce longer holds.

Exercises
- Bird‑dog with diagonal reach and pelvic floor cue: 3 × 8 per side.
- Pallof press (isometric, light band or pressing a towel in doorway) — emphasis on breathing: 3 × 8–10 per side.
- Plank progression (forearm plank from knees → half plank from toes): 3 × 20–30 sec (watch for doming).
- Dead bug progression (increase ROM): 3 × 10 per side.
- Standing anti‑rotation chops (light, slow): 3 × 8–10 per side.

Phase C — Weeks 11–12+: Anterior core reintroduction and more dynamic control
Goals: allow gentle flexion work and longer sustained core holds; introduce light loaded or dynamic core moves if tolerated.

Exercises
- Short curl pattern (NOT full sit‑up): supine, chin tuck, lift head/shoulders 1–2 inches while bracing — 3 × 10 (stop if doming).
- Plank progressions: forearm plank from toes up to 30–60 sec total across sets or knees to toes transition: 3 sets.
- Side plank full from knees → toes: 3 × 20–40 sec per side.
- Dead bug with small ankle weight or small resistance: 3 × 8–10 per side.
- Pallof press with increased hold time and controlled eccentric: 3 × 10 per side.
- Controlled bicycle/oblique rotations (slow, small ROM) for 2–3 sets × 10 per side, only if no bulge.

Guidelines on specific exercises to avoid early

- Hip hinge + carry (pick & carry backpack) 3 rounds
- Lateral lunges 3×8/side

- Plank holds progression, side planks, dead bug variations as above.

Cardio (3–5×/week)
- 1 longer brisk walk 30–40 min
- 1–2 interval sessions: increase to 8 rounds of 60–90 sec brisk / 60–75 sec recovery
- 1–2 recovery walks 20 min

Nutrition & recovery
- Continue breastfeeding caloric needs; add 150–300 kcal on heavier strength days if tired.
- Post‑workout protein 20–30 g within 60 min.

- RPE 6–8 on key strength sets. Rep ranges: 6–10 for compound, 8–15 accessory.
- Rest 45–90 sec depending on load. Maintain diaphragmatic breathing and light pelvic‑floor brace.

Session A – Lower strength (45 min)
- Warm up 7–8 min
- Breathing cue 3–4 reps
- Goblet squat (backpack): 4×8 (3s eccentric)
- Romanian deadlift (backpack) 3×8
- Bulgarian split squat 3×8/leg superset with glute bridge 3×12
- Farmer carries: 4×40–60 sec (heavier)
- Core: Pallof press 3×10/side
- Cool down

Session B – Upper & core (45 min)
- Warm up
- Push progression: 4×6–10 push‑ups (incline → knees → floor as ready)
- Bent‑over row (heavier) 4×8–10
- Overhead press (backpack or bottles) 3×8–10
- Dead bug + side plank superset: 3×10/side + 3×20–30 sec
- Conditioning finisher: 3 rounds 45 sec marching/low step / 30 sec rest
- Cool down

Session C – Functional & conditioning (45–50 min)
- Warm up
- Circuit 3 rounds: 8 deadlifts (backpack), 8 reverse lunges/leg, 8 push reps, 30 sec Pallof hold — rest 90 sec between rounds
- Farmer carry heavy 3×60 sec
- Plank total 60 sec (build across sets)
- Cool down & safe baby‑lift practice

Cardio (3–5×/week)
- 2 brisk walks 30–45 min (inclines optional)
- 1 interval session: 8–10 rounds 90 sec brisk / 60 sec easy (low impact)
- 1 recovery walk 20 min

Week 12 (peak intensity for 12‑week mark, and first possible low‑impact HIIT if all clear)
Session A – Lower strength heavy set (45–50 min)
- Warm up 8 min
- Goblet squats: 1 heavier set × 6 reps (challenging but safe), then 2×8
- Romanian deadlifts: 3×6–8 (increased load)
- Split squats or reverse lunges 3×8/leg
- Farmer carry heavy: 4×60 sec
- Core: plank pyramid 20/30/40 sec (total 90s) — stop if doming
- Cool down

Session B – Upper power & volume (45 min)
- Warm up
- Push: 3 sets × 6–8 full push‑ups or challenging progression
- Bent‑over row heavier 4×6–8
- Overhead press 3×6–8
- Superset: Pallof press 3×10 + side plank 3×30 sec
- Conditioning finisher: 4 rounds 40 sec step‑ups / 20 sec rest
- Cool down

Session C – Functional metabolic & carries (45–50 min)
- Warm up
- EMOM mini circuit 12 min (every minute perform set then rest remainder):
  - Min 1: 8 goblet squats
  - Min 2: 8 Romanian deadlifts
  - Min 3: 8 incline push‑ups
- Rest 2 min
- Carry complex: 3 rounds 60 sec farmer carry + 30 sec suitcase carry each side
- Core: dead bug loaded 3×10/side
- Cool down

Cardio & HIIT (Week 12 only HIIT if all pelvic‑floor/core checks clear)
- Cardio frequency 3–5×/wk: 2 brisk walks (30–45 min), 1 interval session
- Low‑impact HIIT session (once/week max; start cautiously — total high‑intensity ≤10–12 min)
  - Example: 8 rounds 30 sec fast marching high knees / 45 sec easy march
  - Or circuit 3 rounds: 40 sec step‑ups, 40 sec incline mountain climbers (hands on counter), 60 sec rest
  - Keep RPE ≤8 and monitor for leakage/dom­ing next 24–48 hrs.

Core progression (weeks 7–12 integrated)
- Weeks 7–8: diaphragmatic breathing, supine brace, heel slides, dead bug small ROM, side planks knees.
- Weeks 9–10: increase ROM/dead bug, Pallof presses, forearm plank from knees → toes up to 30 sec, gentle curl pattern trials if no doming.
- Weeks 11–12: include short curl pattern 3×10, plank progressions up to 60s total, Pallof holds, loaded dead bug if tolerated. Avoid heavy loaded sit‑ups and straight leg raises unless pelvic‑floor physio cleared.

HIIT progression (if pursued beyond week 12)
- Earliest recommended HIIT start: week 13+ and only if all signs good. Start low‑impact HIIT 1×/week and progress 4 weeks before adding higher impact. Always keep pelvic‑floor clearance in mind.

Nutrition plan (integrated)
- Targets: start ~2,200–2,800 kcal/day depending on body size/activity and breastfeeding. Aim for gradual weight loss (0.25–0.5 kg/week) only if desired and milk supply maintained.
- Protein: 1.2–1.6 g/kg/day (e.g., for 70 kg: 84–112 g/day).
- Carbohydrate: 45–55% of calories — whole grains, fruit, starchy veg.
- Fat: 25–35% of calories with omega‑3 DHA emphasis (200–300 mg/day).
- Micronutrients: iron, calcium, vitamin D, iodine — monitor and supplement per clinician.
- Hydration: 2.5–3.5 L/day; sip during feeds; limit caffeine <300 mg/day.
- Meal pattern: 3 meals + 2–3 snacks. Pre/post workout snacks: banana + nut butter before; Greek yogurt or smoothie after.
- Increase calories slightly on heavy strength/HIIT days (+150–300 kcal) to support energy and milk supply.

- Scar massage: begin only after incision fully healed and clinician approval (~6+ weeks). Gentle circular massage 2–3 min daily if comfortable.
- Strongly recommend referral to pelvic‑floor physiotherapist if any leakage, pelvic heaviness, large DR (>2–3 finger width), or persistent pain.

- How slept? (good / poor)
- Any urine/fecal leakage today? (yes/no)
- Any pelvic heaviness? (yes/no)
- Any incision pain or increased tenderness? (yes/no)
- Energy level (1–10)
If any pelvic symptoms or incision issues → avoid progressing; regress to walking/ gentle breathing/core and seek physio/OB advice.

Example micro‑progressions you can apply
- If client performs 3×10 bodyweight squats pain‑free for 2 weeks, add a 4th set or 2–4 kg in backpack.
- If pelvic floor symptoms appear after a session, reduce intensity next session by 30–50% and remove any loaded carries.

Documentation & coaching tips for you
- Keep short symptom log after sessions for first 12 weeks (bleeding, leakage, doming, pain). Adjust plan if red flags appear.
- Time workouts after feeds/pumping to avoid engorgement and discomfort.
- Praise functional wins: carrying baby comfortably, no leakage when coughing, longer walks with good breathing.

- Video cues or written cue cards for each exercise and regressions/progressions.
- A tailored calorie and meal plan using the client’s exact bodyweight and breastfeeding frequency.

Below is the complete 12‑week postpartum return programme for your 33‑year‑old client who is 4 weeks post uncomplicated C‑section and currently cleared only for light activity (walking; no abs/ heavy lifting until 6‑week check). This plan rolls in everything we discussed: phased movement progression, core return, progressive strength (home only, mat and household items optional), cardio and HIIT introductions, breastfeeding‑supportive nutrition, recovery and pelvic‑floor safeguards. Use it as a guide and modify to the client’s signs, symptoms and OB / pelvic‑floor physiotherapist recommendations.

Important safety prefaces (read to client and follow every session)
- Only begin strength, targeted core or higher intensity cardio/HIIT after OB clearance at 6 weeks.
- Stop any exercise and refer to clinician if you see or feel: heavy/ increasing bleeding, fever, worsening incision pain, new or worsening pelvic heaviness/pressure, urine/fecal leakage, or doming/coning (bulging) along the midline with effort.
- Always cue diaphragmatic breathing and a light pelvic‑floor contraction before exertion (no breath‑holding or bearing down).
- If diastasis recti (DR) or pelvic‑floor dysfunction is present, prioritize pelvic‑floor physiotherapy; regress core and impact progressions as needed.
- Nutrition: follow breastfeeding‑supportive guidance (approx. 2,200–2,800 kcal/day as a starting estimate depending on size/activity; protein 1.2–1.6 g/kg; hydrate 2.5–3.5 L/day). Increase calories modestly on heavier days. Continue prenatal/postnatal vitamins as advised.

Structure overview
- Weeks 4–6 (Phase 1): Recovery & re‑establish breathing/pelvic floor — low intensity only. Frequency: daily walking + 3 short movement sessions/week.
- Weeks 7–10 (Phase 2): After 6‑wk clearance, progressive strength & core re‑education, introduce low‑impact cardio intervals. Frequency: 3 strength sessions/week + 3–5 cardio sessions/week + 2–3 core mini sessions/week.
- Weeks 11–12 (Phase 3 — push intensity): Progress to higher intensity strength, carries, conditioning, longer cardio and optional low‑impact HIIT introduction only if pelvic floor/no doming. Frequency: 3 strength sessions/week + 3–5 cardio sessions/week + 1 low‑impact HIIT/week (or short conditioning finishers).

Weekly time commitment
- Weeks 4–6: Sessions ~20–30 min; daily short walks 10–30 min.
- Weeks 7–10: Sessions ~30–40 min; cardio up to 30–40 min.
- Weeks 11–12: Sessions ~40–50 min; cardio/conditioning increased (HIIT short and controlled).

Progression principles
- Progress reps → sets → ROM → load → tempo/complexity.
- Increase only if pain‑free, no pelvic‑floor signs and client feels recovered.
- Use RPE and symptoms rather than pushing by schedule if tired or breastfeeding demands increase.

Now the full week‑by‑week plan. Each week lists 3 structured strength sessions (A,B,C), suggested core work, cardio plan, and nutrition/recovery reminders.

Weeks 4 (current) – 6 (Phase 1: safe recovery; pre‑clearance through week 6)
Main goals: walking, diaphragmatic breathing, gentle pelvic‑floor awareness, posture, shoulder/hip mobility, glute activation. No abdominal loading or heavy lifting.

Session format (do 3×/week: Sessions A/B/C have the same template in weeks 4–5; slightly progress week 6 only if OB allows)
Session A / B / C (20–25 min)
- Warm up 4–6 min: gentle marching or short walk; shoulder rolls.
- Diaphragmatic breathing + pelvic floor cue: 4–6 breaths (gently lift pelvic floor 1–2 sec on exhale).
- Pelvic floor quicks: 6–8 quick squeezes.
- Modified glute bridge (small range): 2×8–10
- Clamshells side‑lying: 2×10 per side
- Wall push‑ups: 2×8–10
- Hip hinge practice (supine bridging/hip hinge drills): 2×8
- Cool down: gentle stretch 3–5 min

Cardio (daily)
- Gentle walks 10–20 min as tolerated. Keep RPE 1–3. Break into small walks across the day if needed.

Nutrition & recovery
- Start with breastfeeding‑supportive calories ~2,200–2,600 kcal/day depending on size and activity. Ensure protein at each meal.
- Hydrate, rest after feeds, avoid heavy lifting (ask for help with car seats), and keep incision care per OB instructions.
- No scar massage until incision fully healed/clinician approval (~6 weeks).

Week 6 (if OB still requires only light activity, continue Phase 1 protocol). If OB clears at 6 weeks, start Week 7 progression. Prior to Week 7, perform quick screening: cough, heel‑slide and supine brace tests; if any leakage, doming or heaviness — continue conservative progress and refer to pelvic‑floor physiotherapist.

Weeks 7–8 (Phase 2a: foundational strength + core re‑education)
Main goals: begin structured strength, retrain transverse abdominis, anti‑extension/rotation, continue walking. Light external loads only if pelvic floor fine.

Strength: 3 sessions/week (A, B, C). Session length 30–35 min.

Week 7 sample
Session A – Lower focus (30–35 min)
- Warm up 5–7 min brisk walk + mobility
- Diaphragmatic breathing + pelvic floor holds: 4×4 sec
- Glute bridge → progress to full range: 3×10
- Bodyweight squat to chair: 3×10–12
- Box/step‑up low: 3×8 per leg
- Standing calf raises: 3×12–15
- Cool down & breathing

Session B – Upper & core (30 min)
- Warm up 5 min
- Wall/incline push‑ups: 3×10
- Seated towel row: 3×10
- Bird‑dog: 3×8 per side
- Dead bug (small ROM): 3×8 per side
- Side plank from knees: 2×15–20 sec per side
- Cool down

Session C – Posterior chain & mobility (30–35 min)
- Warm up
- Hip hinge practice (bodyweight RDL pattern): 3×10
- Reverse lunges: 3×8 per leg
- Clamshells: 3×12 per side
- Farmer carry practice (light object; short 30–45 sec holds): 3 rounds
- Gentle chest/hip flexor stretches

Core mini work (2–3×/week) — low load
- Diaphragmatic breathing/ pelvic floor cues: 4×5 breaths
- Supine brace holds 5–8 sec × 6
- Heel slides small ROM: 2 sets × 8–10 per side

Cardio (3–5×/week)
- 3 easy–brisk walks/week 20–30 min
- 1 optional short low‑impact interval: 6×60 sec brisk / 90 sec easy (as tolerated) — keep RPE ≤6 on brisk efforts.

Nutrition & recovery
- Protein target ~1.2–1.6 g/kg/day; include protein in post‑workout snack.
- Hydration and snacks timed around feeds and workouts.

Week 8: Progress by adding 1–2 reps per set or an additional set on key exercises; increase walk length to 25–35 min on one day. Continue same core progressions.

Weeks 9–10 (Phase 2b: increase load, unilateral work, tempo)
Main goals: increase volume, introduce light household load, unilateral strength, longer core holds and low‑impact cardio intervals.

Strength: 3 sessions/week. Session length ~35–40 min.

Week 9 sample
Session A – Lower (35–40 min)
- Warm up 7 min
- Pelvic floor breathing 4×5 sec
- Single‑leg Romanian deadlift (bodyweight → light water bottle) 3×8–10/leg
- Bulgarian split squat or elevated rear foot 3×8/leg
- Goblet squat (light backpack/water bottle at chest) 3×10 (3s descent)
- Glute bridge with 2s hold 3×12
- Calf raises single leg 3×10
- Cool down & scar mobility if cleared

Session B – Upper & core (35 min)
- Warm up
- Incline/ knee push‑ups → progress 3×8–12
- Bent‑over row (backpack) 3×10
- Pallof press (isometric) 3×8–10/side
- Dead bug progression (increase ROM) 3×10/side
- Farmer carry (moderate) 4×40–60 sec
- Cool down

Session C – Full body functional (35–40 min)
- Warm up
- Step‑ups with knee drive 3×8/leg
- Hip hinge + carry (pick & carry backpack) 3 rounds
- Lateral lunges 3×8/side
- Plank progression: forearm from knees → 3×20–30 sec
- Low‑impact conditioning finisher: 2–3 rounds of 60 sec marching / 30 sec rest
- Cool down

Core (2–3×/week)
- Plank holds progression, side planks, dead bug variations as above.
- Begin short curl pattern trials in Week 10 only if no doming/leakage and heel‑slide/dead bug tests are perfect.

Cardio (3–5×/week)
- 1 longer brisk walk 30–40 min
- 1–2 interval sessions: increase to 8 rounds of 60–90 sec brisk / 60–75 sec recovery
- 1–2 recovery walks 20 min

Nutrition & recovery
- Continue breastfeeding caloric needs; add 150–300 kcal on heavier strength days if tired.
- Post‑workout protein 20–30 g within 60 min.

Weeks 11–12 (Phase 3: push intensity — targeted strength, conditioning, low‑impact HIIT possible)
Prerequisites: OB cleared at 6 weeks, no leakage, no pelvic heaviness, no doming during core tests, comfortable with single‑leg drills and 30–60s plank holds. If any condition unmet, delay intensity and consult pelvic‑floor physio.

Goals: create a feeling of strength and readiness — heavier sets, carries, denser conditioning, one short HIIT session (low‑impact) introduced in Week 12 only if all signs good. Continue core progressions focused on control and brief anterior work.

General intensity targets
- RPE 6–8 on key strength sets. Rep ranges: 6–10 for compound, 8–15 accessory.
- Rest 45–90 sec depending on load. Maintain diaphragmatic breathing and light pelvic‑floor brace.

Week 11 (build intensity)
Session A – Lower strength (45 min)
- Warm up 7–8 min
- Breathing cue 3–4 reps
- Goblet squat (backpack): 4×8 (3s eccentric)
- Romanian deadlift (backpack) 3×8
- Bulgarian split squat 3×8/leg superset with glute bridge 3×12
- Farmer carries: 4×40–60 sec (heavier)
- Core: Pallof press 3×10/side
- Cool down

Session B – Upper & core (45 min)
- Warm up
- Push progression: 4×6–10 push‑ups (incline → knees → floor as ready)
- Bent‑over row (heavier) 4×8–10
- Overhead press (backpack or bottles) 3×8–10
- Dead bug + side plank superset: 3×10/side + 3×20–30 sec
- Conditioning finisher: 3 rounds 45 sec marching/low step / 30 sec rest
- Cool down

Session C – Functional & conditioning (45–50 min)
- Warm up
- Circuit 3 rounds: 8 deadlifts (backpack), 8 reverse lunges/leg, 8 push reps, 30 sec Pallof hold — rest 90 sec between rounds
- Farmer carry heavy 3×60 sec
- Plank total 60 sec (build across sets)
- Cool down & safe baby‑lift practice

Cardio (3–5×/week)
- 2 brisk walks 30–45 min (inclines optional)
- 1 interval session: 8–10 rounds 90 sec brisk / 60 sec easy (low impact)
- 1 recovery walk 20 min

Week 12 (peak intensity for 12‑week mark, and first possible low‑impact HIIT if all clear)
Session A – Lower strength heavy set (45–50 min)
- Warm up 8 min
- Goblet squats: 1 heavier set × 6 reps (challenging but safe), then 2×8
- Romanian deadlifts: 3×6–8 (increased load)
- Split squats or reverse lunges 3×8/leg
- Farmer carry heavy: 4×60 sec
- Core: plank pyramid 20/30/40 sec (total 90s) — stop if doming
- Cool down

Session B – Upper power & volume (45 min)
- Warm up
- Push: 3 sets × 6–8 full push‑ups or challenging progression
- Bent‑over row heavier 4×6–8
- Overhead press 3×6–8
- Superset: Pallof press 3×10 + side plank 3×30 sec
- Conditioning finisher: 4 rounds 40 sec step‑ups / 20 sec rest
- Cool down

Session C – Functional metabolic & carries (45–50 min)
- Warm up
- EMOM mini circuit 12 min (every minute perform set then rest remainder):
  - Min 1: 8 goblet squats
  - Min 2: 8 Romanian deadlifts
  - Min 3: 8 incline push‑ups
- Rest 2 min
- Carry complex: 3 rounds 60 sec farmer carry + 30 sec suitcase carry each side
- Core: dead bug loaded 3×10/side
- Cool down

Cardio & HIIT (Week 12 only HIIT if all pelvic‑floor/core checks clear)
- Cardio frequency 3–5×/wk: 2 brisk walks (30–45 min), 1 interval session
- Low‑impact HIIT session (once/week max; start cautiously — total high‑intensity ≤10–12 min)
  - Example: 8 rounds 30 sec fast marching high knees / 45 sec easy march
  - Or circuit 3 rounds: 40 sec step‑ups, 40 sec incline mountain climbers (hands on counter), 60 sec rest
  - Keep RPE ≤8 and monitor for leakage/dom­ing next 24–48 hrs.

Core progression (weeks 7–12 integrated)
- Weeks 7–8: diaphragmatic breathing, supine brace, heel slides, dead bug small ROM, side planks knees.
- Weeks 9–10: increase ROM/dead bug, Pallof presses, forearm plank from knees → toes up to 30 sec, gentle curl pattern trials if no doming.
- Weeks 11–12: include short curl pattern 3×10, plank progressions up to 60s total, Pallof holds, loaded dead bug if tolerated. Avoid heavy loaded sit‑ups and straight leg raises unless pelvic‑floor physio cleared.

HIIT progression (if pursued beyond week 12)
- Earliest recommended HIIT start: week 13+ and only if all signs good. Start low‑impact HIIT 1×/week and progress 4 weeks before adding higher impact. Always keep pelvic‑floor clearance in mind.

Nutrition plan (integrated)
- Targets: start ~2,200–2,800 kcal/day depending on body size/activity and breastfeeding. Aim for gradual weight loss (0.25–0.5 kg/week) only if desired and milk supply maintained.
- Protein: 1.2–1.6 g/kg/day (e.g., for 70 kg: 84–112 g/day).
- Carbohydrate: 45–55% of calories — whole grains, fruit, starchy veg.
- Fat: 25–35% of calories with omega‑3 DHA emphasis (200–300 mg/day).
- Micronutrients: iron, calcium, vitamin D, iodine — monitor and supplement per clinician.
- Hydration: 2.5–3.5 L/day; sip during feeds; limit caffeine <300 mg/day.
- Meal pattern: 3 meals + 2–3 snacks. Pre/post workout snacks: banana + nut butter before; Greek yogurt or smoothie after.
- Increase calories slightly on heavy strength/HIIT days (+150–300 kcal) to support energy and milk supply.

Scar care & pelvic floor physiotherapy
- Scar massage: begin only after incision fully healed and clinician approval (~6+ weeks). Gentle circular massage 2–3 min daily if comfortable.
- Strongly recommend referral to pelvic‑floor physiotherapist if any leakage, pelvic heaviness, large DR (>2–3 finger width), or persistent pain.

Daily readiness checklist (use before sessions)
- How slept? (good / poor)
- Any urine/fecal leakage today? (yes/no)
- Any pelvic heaviness? (yes/no)
- Any incision pain or increased tenderness? (yes/no)
- Energy level (1–10)
If any pelvic symptoms or incision issues → avoid progressing; regress to walking/ gentle breathing/core and seek physio/OB advice.

Example micro‑progressions you can apply
- If client performs 3×10 bodyweight squats pain‑free for 2 weeks, add a 4th set or 2–4 kg in backpack.
- If pelvic floor symptoms appear after a session, reduce intensity next session by 30–50% and remove any loaded carries.

Documentation & coaching tips for you
- Keep short symptom log after sessions for first 12 weeks (bleeding, leakage, doming, pain). Adjust plan if red flags appear.
- Time workouts after feeds/pumping to avoid engorgement and discomfort.
- Praise functional wins: carrying baby comfortably, no leakage when coughing, longer walks with good breathing.

If you want next:
- A printable calendar checklist for each week with daily sessions tick boxes.
- Video cues or written cue cards for each exercise and regressions/progressions.
- A tailored calorie and meal plan using the client’s exact bodyweight and breastfeeding frequency.
